bullets.title: Fed hiking cycle re-accelerating: 100bp cumulative by Apr 2027 now base case
bullets.body: October core CPI printed +0.3% m/m for the third straight month, while PPI came in at 6.5% y/y (cycle high). NY Fed's Williams described inflation as 'far' too high and signaled steady small hikes ahead; Fed Governor Waller said a third straight 0.3% core print puts 50bp December on the table; Dallas Fed's Logan called for at least two more hikes at a faster pace. Markets now price ~85bp of hikes through end-2027 (up 39bp w/w) and a 13% chance of 50bp in December, though softer PPI components pulled core PCE tracking down ~4-6bp to ~0.29% m/m, keeping 50bp a tail risk rather than base case.

bullets.title: 10-year yield above 5.15%; 2Y had worst week in 2 years on hawkish repricing
bullets.body: Front-end yields surged ~30bp w/w — the 2-year's worst weekly move in two years. The 10-year is now approaching the 5.15–5.185% retracement level with longer-term support at 5.25–5.35%. JPM's fair-value model shows yields only modestly below fair value (-4bp residual), removing the chronic undervaluation narrative that had supported duration longs.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang forced out as NVDA CEO; DOJ probe, China intelligence ties cited
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA President/CEO effective immediately following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset and a DOJ probe; Colette Kress named interim CEO. The departure triggered multiple sell-side downgrades (HSBC to Hold, $170 PT from $365; Bernstein to Market-Perform at $200; GS cut PT to $220 from $300) and $500bn in market cap loss on ~2bn shares traded (~8% of float) this week. Retail aggressively bought the dip — $111M in first 30 minutes Thursday, a 40x normal volume, 9-standard-deviation move — with bulls citing ~10x CY27 GAAP EPS as depressed valuation.

bullets.title: NVDA leadership vacuum creates ecosystem financing risk; Kress opposed Huang's $250B backstop
bullets.body: Incoming interim CEO Colette Kress had resisted Huang's largest AI financing plans, including a $250B OpenAI backstop, and NVDA's $164B total financial commitments are under review. Morgan Stanley notes the leadership change could impair neocloud financing and favor larger hyperscalers; credit markets priced roughly flat (spreads unchanged to slightly tighter), implying expectations for greater balance sheet discipline and less ecosystem backstopping — which could slow infrastructure investment among speculative issuers.

bullets.title: China AI export controls tightening; Congressional probes to run into next year
bullets.body: Huang's resignation is accelerating Commerce Department finalization of tighter export restrictions, including offshore compute access across seven additional countries. The Megaspeed chip diversion scandal has pushed FY27 defense authorization into the 120th Congress, with Senate estimates of a $500–700bn gap in Pentagon appropriations. The AI OVERWATCH Act, Remote Access Security Act, and Chip Security Act are advancing; the MATCH Act represents the greatest escalation risk to the US-China tech truce, which the base case assumes survives but under increasing strain.

bullets.title: AI supply-chain rotation: AMD/AVGO gain ~$500bn combined as NVDA loses same
bullets.body: AMD and AVGO are the only two AI supply-chain stocks near 52-week highs; AMD +5.9% and AVGO +5.5% on the week as investors rotated from NVDA. AMAT also screens attractively at 14x CY28 EPS vs a 10-year average 17x, with GS expecting WFE growth to accelerate to ~45% y/y in 2027. Meaningful AI datacenter revenue reductions are already priced into electronics/test stocks (APH, KEYS, TEL, BDC), while VRT, FLEX, JBL face higher estimate-reduction risk given heavier AI infrastructure exposure.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO: ~6x oversubscribed at $1.5T valuation, targeting ~$61B raise on Nov 19
bullets.body: Anthropic's IPO is priced at $70–78/share and reportedly 6x oversubscribed, with valuation bumped to $1.5T minimum; the raise would eclipse all IPOs except SpaceX to rank #2 all-time. Q4 revenue is tracking to a high-$70bn annualized run rate (not the $100bn+ target), and 2027 targets appear aggressive. $10–15bn of index-tracking buying is expected in the first four weeks post-listing starting Nov 19.

bullets.title: Broad market technicals deteriorating: breadth weak, semis/AI expected lower
bullets.body: NYSE and NASDAQ are showing new lows and weak breadth; stocks above the 200-day moving average signal the market is not yet oversold. High Beta Momentum is down 45% from June peak and down 7.2% YTD; retail investor baskets are down 30% from May peak. AAII bears are at the 96th percentile; CTAs moved from +150% to -5% global equity exposure. Technical analysis flags AI, memory, and semis as likely to work lower with bond yields moving higher.

bullets.title: SPX pivot at 7,600 with 7,400 support; negative gamma reduced, put skew compressing
bullets.body: S&P futures are +0.4% with the index at ~7,531. Options technicals show negative gamma has been reduced and put skews are coming down relative to call skews — described as an encouraging technical setup. VIX +9.7% to 20.51 on the week with unusual call-skewed options volume across AI, healthcare, and discretionary names.

bullets.title: Housing slump deepening: existing home sales lowest since 2010, mortgage rates near 2000 highs
bullets.body: Existing home sales fell 5.5% to 3.75M in October, the lowest level since 2010. Mortgage rates are at their highest since 2000 (excluding one month in 2023), and the median home price rose just 0.4% y/y — the smallest gain since February. Leading indicators for home improvement also weak: declining paint sales and room measurements point to continued softness in remodel demand through FY28.

bullets.title: Global REITs outperform tech by 14.9ppts during IT drawdowns; self-storage leads
bullets.body: The S&P 500 IT Index fell -16.5% month-to-date through Nov 5 while the FTSE EPRA Nareit Developed Index returned +6.6%. Historically, global REITs outperform tech by 14.9ppts during IT sector drawdowns >10% since 1990. Self-storage is the top-performing REIT sector; US apartment new lease rent growth accelerated in October with coastal and Sunbelt markets improving.

bullets.title: Western Europe and UK central banks facing continued hike pressure amid sticky inflation
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its UK 4Q GDP forecast to 1.5% annualized and expects the BoE to hike in December, with inflation not expected to drop below 4% until September 2027. Western European central banks broadly face continued pressure to hike as energy prices remain elevated and growth stays resilient. UK October headline CPI is expected to accelerate to 3.8% y/y.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle: 2027 builds insulated, but 2028 faces >20% datacenter pipeline cuts
bullets.body: Street consensus is that midterm fallout represents delays/conditions not cancellations, with 2027 builds insulated as already funded or under construction. However, planned data center construction is reportedly down 20% for 2028 as Mag-8 and neoclouds cut capex; only 199GW of 586GW in the pipeline is considered truly credible per Bernstein. Current market pricing is seen as at odds with expected 30–40%+ capex growth in 2028, and CoreWeave demand continues running well ahead of supply with pricing on new contracts rising materially.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers now 40% of new LT debt issuance; crowding out IG/HY Tech spreads
bullets.body: YTD USD high-grade issuance stands at $232bn for hyperscalers and $42bn for data centers; hyperscalers now represent 40% of new long-term debt issuance versus a historically rounding-error share. Citi flags rising interest expense as an emerging drag on mega-cap tech earnings as companies draw down cash to finance AI capex. 2027 IG TMT issuance is forecast at $675bn, with $450bn AI-related, split evenly between parent-level hyperscaler borrowing and data center/GPU financing.

bullets.title: Memory prices rising 13-20% on AI demand despite weak consumer; enterprise SSD up 15-20% QoQ
bullets.body: Memory manufacturers are planning 15–20% sequential enterprise SSD price increases in 4Q26, with PC DRAM prices rising 13–18% despite weaker consumer demand. AMAT reported Advanced Packaging grew +90% y/y driven by HBM demand in FY26, with Process Control up +50% y/y. AMAT's largest customer is now providing rolling 8-quarter forecasts with no order pushouts.

bullets.title: China domestic AI accelerator TAM to reach $290bn by 2030; local share to hit 83-88%
bullets.body: UBS initiates coverage of China AI accelerators, projecting a Rmb2.0trn (~$290bn) TAM by 2030 with 10M unit shipments. Chinese vendors' combined market share is forecast to reach 83%/88% in 2027/28E, up 40+ percentage points from 2025 levels, as HBM/component supply constraints ease from 2028 and domestic supply chains mature.

bullets.title: ChatGPT Ads hit $1bn ARR with 10K advertisers; Pinterest identified as clearest share donor
bullets.body: OpenAI's ChatGPT Ads reached ~$1bn annualized run rate by August 2026, growing from ~600 to 10,000+ advertisers in seven months. However, only 11% of agencies are buying ChatGPT ads; ROI perception is rated middling (in line with Pinterest/Nextdoor, below Google/Instagram/TikTok). Pinterest is identified as the clearest share donor, with more agencies planning to cut than add spend there in 2026-2027.

bullets.title: MSFT Outlook outage (~16 hrs) was infrastructure overload, not cyberattack; cybersecurity stocks rally
bullets.body: Microsoft's O365 outage stemmed from a server rollout spiking CPU usage, not a cybersecurity breach. The incident drove cybersecurity stocks higher in pre-market: PANW +3.7% (KeyBanc upgrade), CRWD +3.4%, NET +2.4%. Separately, AI-powered cyberattacks are compressing sophisticated attack timelines from weeks to ~20 minutes, with Wiz noting October saw unprecedented cyber incidents.

bullets.title: Macro regime shift toward Quad 4: Hedgeye shifting positioning from growth to defensive
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags a positioning shift from Quad 2 to Quad 4 for Q4 2026 and 1H 2027 — shorting AI/semis (MEME, DRAM, EWY), metals (Silver -18%, Palladium -24%), and flagging high-beta momentum down 45% from June peak. CTAs moved from +150% to -5% global equity exposure. The 10-year UST TRADE signal is at 5.07% with cycle high at 5.31%.

bullets.title: Upcoming catalysts: NVDA earnings Tuesday PM, Anthropic IPO Thursday, busy retail earnings week
bullets.body: NVDA reports Tuesday post-market with speculation of a possible pre-announcement around the CEO transition. The Anthropic IPO prices Thursday. Major retail earnings include DIS/HD Tuesday, LOW/TGT/TJX Wednesday, BABA/WMT Thursday. MSFT Ignite Conference is Tuesday. The week is expected to be a critical test of whether the AI trade can stabilize around NVDA's fundamentals at ~10x CY27 EPS.
